title: Ribollita Tuscan Twice Boiled Soup

seo.title: Tuscan Ribollita Recipe: Authentic Italian Twice-Boiled Soup
seo.metaDescription: Learn how to make authentic Tuscan Ribollita, a hearty Italian twice-boiled soup. This traditional recipe is packed with vegetables, beans, and bread. Perfect comfort food!

description: Ribollita is a quintessential Tuscan peasant soup, renowned for its hearty, rustic character and the ingenious use of stale bread. This twice-boiled soup is a comforting medley of seasonal vegetables, cannellini beans, and robust Tuscan bread, slowly cooked to perfection. It embodies the rich tradition of cucina povera, transforming humble ingredients into a deeply flavorful and satisfying meal.

ingredients.item: Stale Tuscan bread (or other crusty country bread)

instructions.title: Prepare the Soffritto
instructions.text: Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the chopped onion, carrots, and celery. Cook gently, stirring occasionally, until softened and translucent, about 8-10 minutes.

instructions.title: Add Garlic and Herbs
instructions.text: Stir in the minced garlic, fresh rosemary sprig, and fresh thyme sprig. Cook for another 1-2 minutes until fragrant, being careful not to burn the garlic.

instructions.title: Combine Beans, Tomatoes, and Broth
instructions.text: Add the rinsed cannellini beans, crushed tomatoes, and vegetable broth to the pot. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and let it cook for at least 20 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.

instructions.title: Incorporate the Greens
instructions.text: Uncover the pot and add the chopped kale or savoy cabbage. Stir it into the simmering soup, ensuring it is submerged. Continue to cook for another 10-15 minutes, or until the greens are tender.

instructions.title: The Twice-Boiled Step
instructions.text: Remove the herb sprigs. Stir in the torn stale bread pieces. The bread will absorb the liquid and thicken the soup considerably. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the bread softens and breaks down, creating a thick, porridge-like consistency. This is the 'boiling' (re-heating) step.

instructions.title: Season and Serve
instructions.text: Season the Ribollita generously with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. Ladle the hot soup into bowls. Drizzle with a good quality extra virgin olive oil and, if desired, sprinkle with grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese before serving immediately.

tips: For the best flavor, make Ribollita a day ahead. Reheating it (the 'twice-boiled' part) allows the flavors to deepen and the bread to fully integrate, making it even more delicious.
The type of bread is crucial: use a dense, crusty, day-old Tuscan bread or a similar country-style loaf. Avoid soft sandwich bread, as it will disintegrate too quickly.

Serve Ribollita piping hot, drizzled with a generous amount of high-quality extra virgin olive oil and a sprinkle of freshly ground black pepper. A grating of Parmigiano-Reggiano is a wonderful, though optional, addition.
